title: Why are people climbing out of manholes in NYC? What police say
answer: Videos of groups climbing out of New York City manholes in the early morning have gone viral repeatedly in 2026, most recently in late November. Police have not announced a confirmed motive, but detectives have said they believe many are scavenging the sewers for valuables. The city says entering the sewer system is illegal and extremely dangerous.
body:
The clips look like a movie scene: before dawn, a manhole cover slides open and several people in headlamps and work clothes climb out one by one, then walk off or get into a waiting car. Viewers have nicknamed them "mole people," and comment sections fill with theories ranging from secret tunnels to treasure hunting. Searches like "why are people coming out of manholes" appeared on our radar on Nov. 26.

The pattern goes back months. Police said that one night in May, two separate groups went into manholes in Brooklyn, in Gravesend and Williamsburg, and resurfaced hours later. In August, a TikTok video showed people climbing out of a manhole on Seventh Avenue across from Penn Station shortly after 4 a.m., and it spread nationwide. In September, two men were arrested in Queens and charged with criminal trespassing after going into the sewers, according to Newsweek. The newest wave came this week, when the NYPD released images of six people it wants to question after a group was seen leaving a manhole near Second Avenue and East 17th Street in Manhattan around 5 a.m. with headlamps and shovels.

As for why: detectives told ABC7 they believe the groups are looking for valuables that slip through street grates and collect underground, a theory one person arrested in Queens reportedly echoed to police. After earlier incidents, NYPD emergency officers searched the tunnels and said nothing nefarious was found, and the city's Department of Environmental Protection reported no damage to its equipment. Police have not said the incidents are connected, and as of Nov. 26 no arrests had been announced in the latest case.

For parents and teens who find the videos intriguing: sewers are not an urban adventure. The Department of Environmental Protection warns of toxic gases, sudden flooding and unstable footing, and going in is against the law.
in_the_news: The NYPD released new images on Nov. 26, 2026, of people it wants to question after a group climbed out of a Manhattan manhole near East 17th Street.

faq.q: Who are the people coming out of NYC manholes?
faq.a: Police have not publicly identified them. The NYPD has released images and asked the public for help, and detectives have said many appear to be searching for valuables.

faq.q: Is it illegal to go into a manhole?
faq.a: Yes. New York City says entering the sewer system without authorization is illegal, and two men arrested in Queens in September were charged with criminal trespassing.

faq.q: Why do people call them mole people?
faq.a: It's an internet nickname inspired by the videos and by old urban legends about people living underground in New York. Police have not used the term.

faq.q: Is it dangerous to go into the sewer?
faq.a: Very. City officials warn of toxic gases, confined spaces, unstable surfaces and sudden flooding.
